title: Your evening
tomorrow: Mai misses two days of sitting her first week. ruined already?

cards: Mai's suitcase is zipped and the bus leaves in the morning. Last night at home for six weeks. After dinner, Ông tells her one thing: before you sleep, give the day away.
It sounds like a riddle. It's an old habit. In Vietnamese temples the evening chanting closes with it, and in Ông's house it closes the day.

teach.b: A Buddhist evening has three small moves. First, look back once. Not a trial, just a glance over the day: what helped, what harmed, what you'd keep.
Second, give it away. This is the dedication of merit: whatever good was done today, a kind word, a sit, a meal shared, is wished onward, so it benefits others and not only you.
In Ông's temple the evening chanting closes this way. That's Ông's riddle. You don't hoard the good of a day; you pass it on.
The suttas describe the Buddha lying down on his right side in the lion's posture, mindful, noting the time he'll rise. Then the day is over, and it's allowed to be.
Now the week, all together. A line read slowly, then silence. A friend who holds the same line.
Texts you read yourself. A morning small enough for years. A seat that travels.
And tonight, the day put down.

how: Buddhist evening practice often includes a short review of the day, evening chanting that ends with a dedication of merit to all beings, and lying down mindfully; in Vietnamese temples the evening service closes with the dedication.

o: a long meditation that replaces going to sleep
planning tomorrow's tasks in detail before bed
looking back, giving the good away, then resting

games.q: the week, back again — tap the pairs.
p: friends: not half the path, the whole
the lute, neither too tight nor loose

s: a Buddhist evening practice means a long meditation before bed
three small moves: look back once, give the good away, lie down mindful.
the suttas describe the Buddha lying down on his right side, mindful
the lion's posture, noting the time he'll rise.
giving the day away means trying to forget it
it means wishing its good reaches others. the day is put down, not thrown out.

games.q: your little brother can't sleep, replaying an embarrassing moment from school. what fits today's teaching?
o: look back once, name one good thing too, wish it for someone, then lie down
replay it a few more times until he's found every single mistake
tell him to think about nothing at all until he falls asleep
games.why: the evening looks back once, gives the good away and lies down mindful. the day is put down, not replayed.

practice: Count back through today on your fingers: three things that went well, however small. If you keep the custom, silently wish that any good in them reaches someone else; if not, simply let the list rest.
Then sit, and let the day be put down.

wordCard.voice: Your evening: look back once, give the good away, lie down mindful.

carryVoice: Here's the line: the day put down, with its good given away. A whole week, built.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 3.16 (lying down in the lion's posture, mindful, with the thought of rising)
dedication of merit at the close of chanting (e.g. Khuddakapatha 7 on sharing merit; Vietnamese evening service)
